strengths: The mean-point correspondence is a simple, original hypothesis-generation strategy for a difficult three-view geometry problem. Reusing established five-point and P3P solvers produces a useful, training-free alternative to substantially more complicated methods. The contribution has practical value despite being approximate.

The evaluation is substantial: 90,000 camera triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, two RANSAC implementations, synthetic geometry/noise experiments, and extensive ablations. The supplementary evaluation also considers errors across all three camera pairs, addressing the main metric’s omission of relative translation scale.

Table 2 demonstrates meaningful benefits. The full mean-plus-offset method improves AUC@10 over HC by 3.61, 2.37, and 2.22 percentage points on PhotoTourism, Cambridge, and Aachen. Benefits also survive comparison with an enhanced five-point baseline: on PhotoTourism, the affine method with refinement, filtering, and ENM achieves 76.56 AUC@10 in 32.37 ms, versus 76.20 in 56.52 ms for 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM.

The manuscript explains the approximation and its dependence on refinement, reports unsuccessful variants, provides a source-code link, and specifies important experimental settings. Held-out tuning and component ablations strengthen reproducibility. These supported practical contributions favor weak acceptance despite the efficiency concerns below.
weaknesses: The principal concern is the HC timing comparison. Supplementary Section 8.3, footnote 8, reports approximately 45 ms of model/data loading per RANSAC invocation, a substantial overhead relative to the 60–67 ms HC totals in Table 2. This cost could be amortized across repeated estimates. Moreover, Table 4 reports HC at 66.06 microseconds per solver call, versus 83.92 for the mean-point method and 218.71 for its offset variant. The reported timings therefore do not cleanly establish algorithmic speed superiority over HC when its model remains loaded.

The strongest speed–accuracy claim is incompletely supported against the enhanced five-point baseline. Figure 4 includes 5pt+P3P with and without ENM, but omits its +R+F variants reported in Table 2. Under Table 2’s stopping protocol, the full offset method gains only 0.94 AUC@10 points over the fully enhanced baseline on PhotoTourism while taking 112.60 versus 56.52 ms. The missing matched-budget curves matter for establishing the claimed best trade-off, although useful operating points are already demonstrated.

Robustness remains primarily empirical. Lemma 1 bounds the synthetic correspondence’s epipolar distance by the triangle’s spatial extent; this can be large and does not bound pose error or guarantee successful refinement. Figure 9 confirms approximation bias even with noiseless observations. The assertion that scene dependency becomes negligible after ENM is stronger than the demonstrated evidence, particularly outside the tested landmark scenes and camera configurations.

A narrower reporting issue occurs in Table 6: the Cambridge rows for the affine and mean-point methods with +R+F are identical across every reported quantity, including runtime; their +R+F+ENM rows are likewise identical. These apparent duplicated entries need clarification and limit confidence in those particular ablation comparisons.
